title: RegionDrag: Fast Region-Based Image Editing with Diffusion Models
access_status: full paper (16 PDF pages) and separate supplement (3 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Density of spatial handle–target point pairs derived from region masks
observed_fact: On DragBench-DR the authors randomly subsample point pairs per image. Mean Distance rises as fewer pairs are used. The supplement illustrates the same support-density sweep.
on_off_comparator: Multiple nonzero fractions of the transformed point pairs
response_evidence: Distance versus input fraction; no background-preservation versus achieved-response curve for competing supports.
other_controls_or_scope: Fig. 8 compares initial-only with repeated copy/paste. Main PDF p. 12 specifies α=1 for initial handle-region noise. Supplement Fig. 2 compares that default with α=0, an identifiable on/off pair for a different intervention.

title: Your Latent Mask is Wrong: Pixel-Equivalent Latent Compositing for Diffusion Models
access_status: full paper (10 PDF pages) and separate supplement (8 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Mask-conditioned DecFormer compositor as a whole
locator: Main §4.3, Table 3 and Fig. 5 (Table 3 on PDF p. 7). For mask-head alternatives see Table 1 and Fig. 4. Supplement Apps. A and F, Tables 5–7.
observed_fact: On the same inpainting LoRA, adding DecFormer at every step lowers full-image LPIPS against the target composite from 0.331 to 0.303. Table 3 uses a fixed 30-step setup, common prompts/guidance and COCO validation masks covering more than 15% of the image.
on_off_comparator: Table 3: LoRA alone (no compositor) versus the same LoRA with DecFormer at all 30 steps.
response_evidence: One fixed compositor comparison. Whole-image LPIPS, SSIM, PSNR and FID measure agreement with the target composite.
other_controls_or_scope: The on/off unit is the entire learned compositor, including its residual. The heuristic comparator uses a spatial mask too. The least-squares α in App. A fits target latents; it does not equate realized update magnitudes across editors.

title: Stable Flow: Vital Layers for Training-Free Image Editing
access_status: full paper (12 PDF pages) and separate supplement (26 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Choice of network layers for feature injection
locator: Main §§3.1–3.3, Fig. 3, §4.3 and Table 2 (PDF pp. 3, 6–8). Supplement §2, Figs. 5 and 12.
observed_fact: Layer skipping identifies vital layers. The editing ablation injects features into vital, non-vital or all layers. A separate variant removes latent nudging.
other_controls_or_scope: The authors vary network depth and feature injection. Equal numbers of vital and non-vital layers control the layer count.

title: Taming Rectified Flow for Inversion and Editing
access_status: full paper including appended supplementary sections (15 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Source self-attention value sharing across denoising steps
locator: Main §§3.3 and 4.5, Fig. 7 and Table 5 (PDF pp. 5, 8). See also Apps. B and D.
observed_fact: Fig. 7 varies the number of feature-sharing steps, including zero. The paper recommends five for most image edits. Table 5 tests Taylor solver order at a common evaluation budget.
other_controls_or_scope: Feature sharing changes in time. Matching function-evaluation counts addresses solver cost.

title: FireFlow: Fast Inversion of Rectified Flow for Image Semantic Editing
access_status: full paper including appended supplementary sections (19 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Cached inversion values for attention and number of editing steps
locator: Main §2.3 and method; App. A, Algs. 1–2 (PDF p. 12); App. E, Fig. 8 (pp. 16–17).
observed_fact: FireFlow reuses inversion attention values in editing. Fig. 8 varies the number of editing steps from 2 to 12 and illustrates the changes in the generated edit.
other_controls_or_scope: The varied controls are solver budget and timing of feature reuse.

title: Inversion-Free Image Editing via Rectified Flow
access_status: partial: publisher abstract, section list and supplemental-file listing only; main PDF and supplemental ZIP unavailable
spatial_intervention: Flow consistency sampling, velocity rectification and attention control identified in abstract
locator: IEEE document 11209009, Abstract, start of §I and Supplemental Items (1253.zip); publisher PDF access restricted.

title: DirectEdit: Step-Level Accurate Inversion for Flow-Based Image Editing
access_status: full paper including appended supplementary sections (16 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Spatial edit mask in noise blending
locator: Main Table 1 and Fig. 5 (PDF p. 7), Table 3 (p. 8). App. E.2, Table 4, configurations 6 and 9 (pp. 14–15).
observed_fact: On FLUX, mask-off versus full gives background LPIPS 102.92 versus 35.45 and whole-image CLIP 25.89 versus 25.39 in Table 1 units. Fig. 5 plots separate background-PSNR versus CLIP curves for both mask conditions on FLUX and on SD3.5.
on_off_comparator: Ours (w/o mask) versus Ours on each backbone; fixed comparison plus multiple operating points.
response_evidence: Aggregate preservation–response curves on both backbones. Connected points are different hyperparameter settings. A within-source equal-response estimate is not reported.
other_controls_or_scope: Table 4 separately varies attention injection, direct alignment and other components. The plotted comparison is original-paper evidence.

title: Imagic: Text-Based Real Image Editing with Diffusion Models
access_status: full paper (11 PDF pages) and separate supplement (5 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Interpolation of global text embeddings and denoiser fine-tuning
locator: Main §3, §4.4, Figs. 7–9 (PDF pp. 7–8); supplement App. B, Figs. 13–15.
observed_fact: Fig. 9 averages target CLIP and input-image 1−LPIPS across 150 image–text inputs as the interpolation weight η changes. Fig. 7 compares embedding interpolation before and after model fine-tuning.
other_controls_or_scope: A measured edit/preservation sweep exists for global text interpolation. It does not compare spatial allocations.

title: Null-text Inversion for Editing Real Images Using Guided Diffusion Models
access_status: full paper (10 PDF pages) and separate supplement (13 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Inversion and null-text optimization; local Prompt-to-Prompt editing is used downstream
locator: Main §§4–5, Figs. 4–5 and 7 (PDF pp. 6–7); supplement App. A, Fig. 1 (p. 1).
observed_fact: Supplement Fig. 1 compares SDEdit with and without the proposed inversion at several noise strengths over 100 examples. Its bottom panel shows outputs chosen for equal CLIP. Main Fig. 7 compares different masked editing methods.
other_controls_or_scope: The equal-CLIP example and LPIPS–CLIP curves pertain to inversion. Main Fig. 5 reweights a text token. Neither experiment holds the editor fixed while varying a spatial gate.

title: PnP Inversion: Boosting Diffusion-based Editing with 3 Lines of Code
access_status: full paper including appended supplementary sections (28 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Source/target branch residual corrections and guidance scales
locator: Main §§5.4.1–5.4.2, Tables 4–5 (PDF p. 9); App. C (PIE-Bench masks); App. E.4, Table 10 and Fig. 6 (p. 19).
observed_fact: Table 4 varies the fraction of a latent difference applied to the source branch. Table 5 changes the residual applied to the target branch. Table 10 varies inverse and forward guidance and reports both preservation and CLIP.
other_controls_or_scope: PIE-Bench evaluation masks define where to score errors. Residual scaling is applied to a branch. This is Ju et al.’s ICLR paper, the specified replacement for the 2022 Blended Diffusion paper.

title: Blended Diffusion for Text-driven Editing of Natural Images
access_status: full paper (11 PDF pages) and separate supplement (22 PDF pages)
locator: Main §§4.1–4.2, Figs. 3–4 and Alg. 2 (PDF pp. 3–5); §5.2, Fig. 7. Separate supplement, additional edits and Fig. 20.
observed_fact: The method blends the evolving edited region with the appropriately noised input background. The cited ablation evaluates augmentations in CLIP guidance.
other_controls_or_scope: Published at CVPR 2022 and excluded from the 2023–26 candidate denominator. B10 is the authorized replacement. The 2023 Blended Latent Diffusion paper is a different study.

title: Diffusion Self-Guidance for Controllable Image Generation
access_status: full paper including appended supplementary sections (18 PDF pages)
spatial_intervention: Weights on attention-derived object-shape guidance terms
locator: Main §3, Eq. 9 (PDF p. 5); App. B (guidance weights) and App. C, Figs. 16–17 (pp. 17–18).
observed_fact: Fig. 17 varies five positive weights for each of three loss terms, holding the other two at their middle values. The two illustrated edits enlarge a macaron and move a meatball.
on_off_comparator: Separate positive-weight sweeps for fixing other objects’ shapes and transforming the target shape.
response_evidence: Visual weight sweeps. No measured preservation–response curve for the shape-term comparison.
other_controls_or_scope: The third swept term fixes appearance. Fig. 16 separately compares appearance transfer with unguided sampling. These are spatial-feature objectives, distinct from a pointwise attenuation mask.

title: Zero-shot Image-to-Image Translation
access_status: full paper including appended supplementary sections (21 PDF pages)
locator: Author full paper §3.3, Alg. 1 and Eq. 5; §4.4, Fig. 6 and Table 2 (PDF pp. 8–10); Apps. C–D.
observed_fact: Configurations D and E use the same DDIM inversion, noise regularization and sentence directions. E adds cross-attention guidance. On cat→dog, background LPIPS changes from 0.274 to 0.182, structure distance from 0.095 to 0.044, and CLIP accuracy from 100.0% to 92.4%.
on_off_comparator: Table 2 D versus E; Fig. 6 explicitly shows guidance on/off. One common default guidance weight for these ablations is unspecified.
response_evidence: One reported pair of configurations per task. Simultaneously reporting CLIP and LPIPS does not establish a response-matched pair or curve.
other_controls_or_scope: The loss guides the full spatial attention map. It is not an edit-region gate. The paper specifies a separate noise regularization coefficient.
